target.title: feat(computer-use): control macOS nodes via screenshots and input injection
target.body:
Related: #97333
Related: #97938
Related: #69799
Related: #44759

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw could screenshot a paired macOS node but could not act on it: there was no way for an agent to move the pointer, click, type, scroll, or press keys on a node. Computer-use ("drive the desktop from a screenshot loop") was a repeatedly requested capability (#97333) with no end-to-end path — no input-injection node command, no agent tool, and no permission/arming model to make it safe.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the first end-to-end computer-use path, scoped to macOS nodes, as a bundled `computer-use` plugin plus a native node executor.

- **Node protocol** (`openclaw.node.computer.v1`): a low-risk `computer.status` read (display geometry, cursor, permission state) and a dangerous `computer.input` write (one action: move / click / mouse down·up / drag / scroll / key / type / hold). Screenshots reuse the existing `screen.snapshot`.
- **macOS executor**: the Mac app node handles `computer.*` natively via CoreGraphics event injection, gated behind a new "Allow Computer Control" setting (default off) and Accessibility trust. Pointer coordinates are interpreted in reference-screenshot pixels and mapped back to global screen points, so the model can click where it sees.
- **Plugin**: registers the `computer` agent tool (drives the screenshot→act loop, one action per call, returning a fresh screenshot to the model), and two node-invoke policies. `computer.input` is `dangerous` — it requires operator opt-in via `gateway.nodes.allowCommands` plus per-session approval, with `allow-always` arming the node for a bounded window (`computer arm/disarm/status`).
- **Safety**: screenshots go to the model, not auto-delivered to chat channels (avoids the on-screen-secret leak class in #44759); the executor lives in the app that holds the TCC grants, not an ambient CLI binary (the concern in #69799); screen content is treated as untrusted input (prompt-injection posture documented in the skill and tool description).

Non-goals (follow-ups): provider-native Anthropic `computer_20251124` tool-type transport, Linux/Windows/sandbox-desktop executors, and time-bounded persistent arming beyond the in-window model.

## User Impact

On a paired macOS node with the plugin enabled, "Allow Computer Control" turned on, and `computer.input` opted into `gateway.nodes.allowCommands`, an agent can look at the screen and operate the Mac — click buttons, type into fields, use keyboard shortcuts, scroll, and drag — with an explicit approval/arming gate. It is macOS-only for now and off by default at every layer.

## Evidence

- **Swift (validated locally):** `apps/shared/OpenClawKit` builds clean; the OpenClaw app target compiles (`swift build --target OpenClaw`, 1070/1070). Swift tests pass: `swift test` → 44 tests across `ComputerInputGeometryTests` (coordinate mapping + Codable, 7/7), `ComputerKeyMapTests` (key-name/chord mapping), and `MacNodeModeCoordinatorTests`/`MacNodeRuntimeTests` (caps/command advertisement + dispatch). `swiftformat --lint` clean.
- **TypeScript:** `pnpm test extensions/computer-use` → 29 passed (4 files). Covers the arming gate (`input-policy.test.ts`: not-armed → approval; deny/null → not invoked; allow-once → invoke without arming; allow-always → armed with expiry; already-armed → invoked without approval; non-macOS → rejected), the tool schema + convenience-click translation, arm-state expiry, and plugin registration (two policies + tool + command + keyed store). Package-manifest contract test → 40 passed. `oxfmt --check` clean. Plugin inventory regenerated (`pnpm plugins:inventory:gen`).
- **Live input injection** (CGEvent + Accessibility TCC) requires a real Mac with the app built and Accessibility granted; it is **not** exercised by CI. This is the remaining manual verification gate before land.

Stacked on the Computer Use manifest contract PR (base). Do not land before live-injection verification on a real Mac.

## What Problem This Solves

The Mattermost inbound handler in `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts` builds a verbose log preview with `bodyText.slice(0, 200)`. ## Why This Change Was Made

target.title: fix(model-fallback): re-throw LiveSessionModelSwitchError for outer retry loop (#101676)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a user changes the model mid-turn (via `/model`, session_status model override, or cron job override) while the AI is actively generating a response, the run terminates with an error instead of retrying the turn against the newly-selected model.

**Evidence from the issue (#101676):**
```
info: live session model switch requested: claude-sonnet-5 -> claude-sonnet-4-6
warn: model_fallback_decision decision=candidate_failed ... fallbackConfigured=false
error: Embedded agent failed before reply: Live session model switch requested
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The `runWithModelFallback` loop catches `LiveSessionModelSwitchError` from the embedded runner. When the switch target is not a later fallback candidate, it was wrapping the error as `FailoverError` instead of letting it propagate to the outer retry loop. With no fallbacks configured, this reached `throwFallbackFailureSummary` producing `FallbackSummaryError` — not `LiveSessionModelSwitchError` — so the outer loop never caught it.

**Fix:** When the switch target is not in the candidate list at all (a genuine user-requested switch to a new model), re-throw `LiveSessionModelSwitchError` so the outer retry loop can restart with the new model. When the switch target IS in the candidate list but at a same/earlier position (a stale fallback-conflict switch), preserve the existing failover behavior so the fallback chain can advance to configured candidates.

The outer loop has bounded retries (`MAX_LIVE_SWITCH_RETRIES = 5` for subagents, `2` for main agent), preventing infinite loops. The existing `findLiveSessionModelSwitchRedirectIndex` redirect-to-later-candidate behavior is preserved unchanged.

Risk note: this touches the agent live-switch/fallback boundary. The stale-switch guard from #58496 is preserved via the `isLiveSessionModelSwitchTargetInCandidates` check.

## Evidence

### Live Behavior Proof

The fix is at the control-flow boundary of `runWithModelFallback`. Source-level verification of the three branches:

**Branch 1 — switch target is a later fallback candidate (redirect, unchanged):**

target.title: fix(codex): cap sandbox file copy reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:** Codex sandbox exec-server filesystem `fs/copy` when copying a sandbox file through the app-server fs bridge.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** `fs/readFile` already stats the sandbox path and rejects files above the 512 MiB exec-server read limit before calling `fsBridge.readFile`. The file branch of `copySandboxPath()` also reads the entire source file into memory, but it called `fsBridge.readFile({ filePath: params.sourcePath })` directly after `stat` without applying the same size check.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Copying an oversized sandbox file could make the app-server buffer that file all at once, bypassing the existing memory guard that direct reads use.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Fix classification:** Minimal root-cause fix.
- **Complete shipped solution:** Reuses a single `assertSandboxFileReadWithinLimit()` guard from both `fs/readFile` and the file-copy path. Recursive directory copies now apply the same per-file cap when they recurse into file leaves.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The unsafe buffering boundary was immediately before `copySandboxPath()` reads a source file into memory; the patch enforces the existing read-file contract at that boundary.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** Keeps `CODEX_SANDBOX_EXEC_SERVER_MAX_READ_FILE_BYTES` as the single source of truth for sandbox exec-server in-memory file reads.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** Does not change the 512 MiB limit, introduce streaming copy semantics, alter directory traversal/listing behavior, or broaden sandbox policy permissions.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** Oversized `fs/copy` file operations now fail with the same error used by oversized `fs/readFile`. Normal file copies and recursive directory copies are preserved.
- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk:low`, `area:codex`, `area:sandbox`.
- **Risk explanation:** The diff is limited to the Codex sandbox exec-server filesystem handler plus a focused regression test. It reuses an existing limit and error message instead of introducing a new behavior surface.
- **Why acceptable:** The behavior change only rejects files that already exceed the exec-server's established in-memory read cap.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** Rely on the Codex sandbox exec-server copy path to respect the same in-memory file size limit as direct reads.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** Allowed file copies still call `fsBridge.readFile` and `fsBridge.writeFile`; recursive copies still create directories and copy supported file leaves.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** I did not make the production handler read a real >512 MiB payload into memory. Instead, the live proof uses a sparse 536,870,913-byte sandbox file and confirms the production WebSocket `fs/copy` RPC rejects from `stat` before `fsBridge.readFile` or `fsBridge.writeFile` is invoked.

## Evidence

- **Environment:** Windows Git Bash, Node v22.17.0, pnpm v11.2.2. `pnpm exec` reported the repository's Node engine warning (`wanted >=22.19.0 <23 || >=23.11.0`) before running the focused test/proof.
- **Commands run after this patch:**
  - `git fetch origin main` followed by inspection of `origin/main:extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/filesystem.ts`; latest checked `origin/main` still had the direct `fsBridge.readFile({ filePath: params.sourcePath })` copy path and no `assertSandboxFileReadWithinLimit(sourceStat)` guard.
  - Open-PR duplicate checks: `copySandboxPath`, `CODEX_SANDBOX_EXEC_SERVER_MAX_READ_FILE_BYTES`, and the oversized-read error text each returned 0 open PRs; the `sandbox-exec-server/filesystem` search results were checked with `gh pr diff <pr> --name-only`, and none changed `extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/filesystem.ts` or `extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.fs.test.ts`.
  - `pnpm exec node --import tsx <temporary proof harness>` from the repository root. The harness dynamically imported the production Codex sandbox exec-server, started its local WebSocket JSON-RPC server, created a sparse 536,870,913-byte sandbox file, sent `fs/copy`, and recorded fs bridge call counters.
  - `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-codex-app-server-tools.config.ts --reporter=verbose extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.fs.test.ts`.
  - `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD`.
- **Key results / observations:** Real behavior proof passed, focused Vitest passed, and whitespace checks passed.
  - Real behavior proof transcript, redacted for host temp paths:
    ```text
    Codex sandbox fs/copy oversized-file live proof
    repo_head=7ce35f8e9e2c96ffce4bd4d39482af62b48ab2d7
    source_sandbox_path=/workspace/huge.bin
    source_size_bytes=536870913
    destination_sandbox_path=/workspace/huge-copy.bin
    host_temp_root=<redacted>
    stat_calls=["/workspace/huge.bin"]
    rpc_error="file is too large to read through Codex sandbox exec-server: 536870913 bytes"
    fsBridge.readFile_calls=0
    fsBridge.writeFile_calls=0
    destination_created=false
    proof_result=PASS
    ```
  - Focused Vitest: 1 test file passed, 15 tests passed. The new regression `rejects oversized file copies before buffering through the fs bridge` passed and verifies `readFile`/`writeFile` are not called for an oversized file-copy source.
  - `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` exited 0.
- **Review findings addressed, if any:** RF-001, RF-002, RF-004, and RF-005 are addressed by the real WebSocket `fs/copy` proof transcript above. RF-003 is called out in the compatibility/risk notes: oversized `fs/copy` now intentionally fails with the established in-memory read cap instead of buffering.
- **Regression guardrail:** The sandbox filesystem test suite now covers direct oversized reads and oversized copies side by side, so future changes that reintroduce an unguarded copy read will fail the focused test.
- **Patch quality notes:** Two production call sites share the same helper; no unrelated files, lockfiles, or generated artifacts are included.

target.title: fix(file-transfer): expand Windows-style tilde policy globs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a Windows file-transfer policy edge case where home-relative globs written with Windows path separators, such as `~\Downloads\**`, were treated as literal glob text instead of being expanded to the user's home directory.

The file-transfer policy already supports home-relative patterns through `~/...` and bare `~`. However, Windows users naturally tend to write local paths with backslashes, and `~\...` looked like the Windows equivalent of `~/...` in configuration. Before this change, that form was not recognized by `expandTilde()`, so the policy matcher received a pattern that still began with a literal `~\` prefix.

That created two confusing outcomes:

- `allowReadPaths` or `allowWritePaths` entries such as `~\Downloads\**` could fail to match files that are actually under the user's home directory.
- `denyPaths` entries such as `~\Downloads\**\*.pem` could fail to enforce the intended hard-deny rule, because the deny glob never resolved to the real home-directory path.

In practice, a Windows operator could configure a policy that appears to allow or deny the correct local folder, while file-transfer policy evaluation behaves differently because only the forward-slash tilde form was expanded.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change extends the existing tilde expansion helper to recognize `~\` as the Windows-style equivalent of `~/`.

The fix is intentionally small and stays inside the shared policy normalization path. `normalizeGlobs()` is already used before matching `allowReadPaths`, `allowWritePaths`, and `denyPaths`, so updating `expandTilde()` gives all three policy surfaces the same home-relative behavior without duplicating logic or changing the matcher itself.

Existing behavior is preserved for:

- `~/...` home-relative globs
- bare `~`
- absolute paths
- normal minimatch semantics
- Windows path separator normalization during matching
- deny-before-allow policy precedence

The change only makes a previously unexpanded Windows-style home prefix behave like the already-supported POSIX-style home prefix. This keeps the policy model consistent while avoiding a broader rewrite of path handling or glob evaluation.

## User Impact

Windows users can now configure file-transfer policy globs using familiar Windows separators, for example:

```text
~\Downloads\**
```

and have them resolve against the same home directory target as:

```text
~/Downloads/**
```

This also makes Windows-style hard-deny rules behave as configured, for example `~\Downloads\**\*.pem` now denies matching files under the user's Downloads directory instead of remaining a non-matching literal pattern.

## Live Windows Behavior Proof

Redacted live proof was run on Windows against the production file-transfer policy evaluator, not a mock or an isolated helper test. The proof calls `evaluateFilePolicy()`, which is the shared policy path used by file-transfer node-invoke checks before file fetch/list/write execution. That path normalizes configured globs through `normalizeGlobs()`, expands home prefixes through `expandTilde()`, and then applies deny-before-allow matching.

```text
Windows file-transfer policy live proof
platform=win32
node=v24.15.0
home=<USER_HOME>
config.allowReadPaths=["~\\Downloads\\**"]
config.denyPaths=["~\\Downloads\\**\\*.pem"]
case=ALLOW Windows-style home glob
path=<USER_HOME>\Downloads\shot.png
decision=matched-allow
ok=true
case=DENY Windows-style hard-deny glob
path=<USER_HOME>\Downloads\key.pem
decision=POLICY_DENIED
ok=false
```

This proves both requested behaviors from a real Windows run:

- `~\Downloads\**` resolves as a home-relative allow glob and permits a matching non-denied file.
- `~\Downloads\**\*.pem` resolves as a home-relative deny glob and still wins over the broader allow rule.

## Compatibility / Security-Boundary Note

This PR intentionally changes how existing file-transfer policy strings beginning with `~\` are interpreted. Before this fix, those entries were effectively literal non-matches; after this fix, they become active home-relative policy globs.

That is the intended Windows policy interpretation: a stored config entry such as `~\Downloads\**` already expresses operator intent to target the user's Downloads directory. The change does not add a new wildcard class or bypass deny precedence; it only makes the Windows-style home prefix behave like the already-supported `~/` home prefix.

Because this is a file-access policy surface, the PR includes both allow and hard-deny proof. The deny proof demonstrates that broad Windows-style allow rules still remain constrained by `denyPaths` after expansion.

## Evidence

Live proof command:

```text
PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR=D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw\node_modules node --import tsx --input-type=module <redacted inline policy proof script>
```

Focused validation passed using the repository Vitest runner with hydrated dependencies:

```text
PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR=D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw\node_modules node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/policy.test.ts

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       32 passed (32)
```

Diff hygiene also passed for the touched files:

```text
git diff --check -- extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/policy.ts extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/policy.test.ts
```

The added regression cases cover both directions:

```text
allowReadPaths: ["~\\Downloads\\**"]
path: <home>/Downloads/shot.png
result: matched allow
```

```text
denyPaths: ["~\\Downloads\\**\\*.pem"]
path: <home>/Downloads/key.pem
result: POLICY_DENIED
```

## Summary

- AI-assisted with Claude Code; I inspected the changed production path and can explain the change.
- Compaction safeguard summary and context truncation in `truncateFailureText`, `capCompactionSummary`, `formatRecentTurnsText`, and `formatSummaryContext` now preserves UTF-16 boundaries when the character cap lands between the code units of an emoji or CJK surrogate pair.
- Uses the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` instead of raw `.slice(0, N)` at five truncation sites.

Compaction summaries, failure text, recent-turn text, and summary context are truncated to fit character budgets before being included in the model prompt. When those cap boundaries fall between the two UTF-16 code units of an emoji, the raw `.slice(0, N)` produces a lone surrogate — a malformed string that may cause rendering issues or unexpected model behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper already handles this boundary correctly and is used by 15+ call sites across the codebase. The five truncation sites in `compaction-safeguard.ts` were among the remaining raw-slice sites in `src/agents/`.

target.title: feat(context-engine): add reference context channel
target.body:
Closes #88753

## What Problem This Solves

Context-engine authors need a safe way to provide historical summaries, memories, or retrieved context without encoding that data as fresh current-user input or higher-authority prompt additions. Without a dedicated lane, compacted/reference data can regain too much prompt authority or interfere with provider message constraints.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a narrow `AssembleResult.referenceContext` SDK lane plus a `reference-context` host capability. Native Codex app-server hosts now project that lane into Codex `turn/start.additionalContext` with `kind: "untrusted"`, so Codex owns the lower-authority external-fragment rendering instead of OpenClaw splicing the data into `turn/start.input`.

Embedded OpenClaw runs no longer advertise `reference-context`; they still support `assemble-before-prompt`, but engines that require a true reference-context lane are rejected there until embedded has an equivalent non-message transport.

## User Impact

Context-engine and plugin developers can return historical/reference data separately from executable model-history messages. Users get safer continuity because native Codex receives the reference data through its dedicated additional-context protocol lane while chat-only/current-user prompt text stays focused on the current request.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof from a redacted local OpenClaw `runCodexAppServerAttempt` test using a fake app-server client that captures the outgoing `turn/start` params:

```text
turn/start.input contains current request: true
turn/start.input contains OpenClaw reference context: false
turn/start.additionalContext.openclaw_reference_context.kind: untrusted
turn/start.additionalContext.openclaw_reference_context.value contains reference summary: true
```

Real Codex app-server proof using installed `@openai/codex` 0.142.4, `codex app-server --listen stdio://`, isolated `CODEX_HOME`, and a local mock `/v1/responses` server:

```text
responseRequestCount: 1
model request contains current prompt "inspect tab": true
model request contains external reference fragment: true
external fragment:
<external_openclaw_reference_context>OpenClaw reference context for this turn:
- Reference note: browser tab title is Example Domain.</external_openclaw_reference_context>

model input item summary:
- developer instructions item
- AGENTS/environment context item
- separate user item with <external_openclaw_reference_context>...</external_openclaw_reference_context>
- separate current user item: inspect tab
```

Additional real Codex app-server clear/replace proof with the same installed app-server and mock `/v1/responses` server:

```text
turn 1 additionalContext value: Reference A
turn 1 user text order: ... external Reference A, first turn

turn 2 additionalContext value: Reference B
turn 2 user text order: ... external Reference A, first turn, external Reference B, second turn

turn 3 additionalContext omitted
turn 3 user text order: ... external Reference A, first turn, external Reference B, second turn, third turn no reference
thirdTurnHasNewExternalImmediatelyBeforePrompt: false
```

That matches Codex core behavior: `AdditionalContextStore::merge(values)` replaces the retained map with the current turn's map, and omitted app-server `additionalContext` maps to an empty map. Prior external fragments remain only as ordinary earlier transcript history; no fresh `openclaw_reference_context` fragment is injected before the current prompt when OpenClaw omits reference context.

Codex source contract checked locally in sibling `../codex`:

- `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs` defines experimental `turn/start.additionalContext` as camelCase `additionalContext`.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs` maps omitted `additionalContext` to an empty core map.
- `codex-rs/core/src/state/additional_context.rs` replaces the retained additional-context map on each turn.
- `codex-rs/context-fragments/src/additional_context.rs` renders untrusted entries as `<external_{key}>...</external_{key}>` fragments.
- `codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/turn_start.rs` covers `turn_start_additional_context_flows_to_model_input`.

target.title: feat(commands): surface live MCP session state in /mcp show
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/mcp show` only ever prints the static `mcp.servers` config. When an MCP
server fails to connect, or connected but the session's config changed
since, the command gives no signal of that: the static config was never
wrong, so users end up debugging config that's fine while the actual
problem — a broken MCP runtime — stays invisible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded-agent MCP runtime already tracks per-session connect/catalog/
failure state through `peekSessionMcpRuntime()` + `SessionMcpRuntime
.peekCatalog()` + `resolveSessionMcpConfigSummary()` — all three read-only
and session-scoped, never creating a runtime, connecting a transport, or
issuing an MCP request. This is the same primitives and peek-without-
connecting pattern the `tools.effective` gateway method already uses
(`src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.ts`), imported through the
same existing public facade (`agents/agent-bundle-mcp-tools.js`) that
method and `session.ts` already use — no new module, no new access path,
and no new load-time cost (that facade is already resident on every
message via `get-reply.ts` → `session.ts`).

This PR threads that already-reachable state into `/mcp show`'s reply as a
separate "🩺 Live state (session)" block, one line per configured server:
`♻️ config changed since last connect (stale)`, `🚫 disabled (enabled:
false, excluded from runtime)`, `✅ connected (N tools)`, `⚠️ <last connect
diagnostic>`, or `⏳ not yet discovered` — in that precedence order, so a
config edit is reported as staleness even for servers whose catalog entry
is still cold. "Stale" compares against the full merged session MCP config
fingerprint (static `mcp.servers` plus any plugin/bundle-contributed
servers), not a per-server diff, so one config edit anywhere in that set
marks every displayed server stale together.

It is purely observational: no daemon/protocol surface was added, no new
persistent state, and no change to `/mcp set|unset` behavior or MCP config
semantics. When no `SessionMcpRuntime` exists yet for the current chat
session, `/mcp show`'s output is byte-identical to before this PR —
verified with an exact-text assertion, not just a substring check.

Non-goals:
- The tool-call failure backoff/pause counter (`serverBackoff` inside
  `createSessionMcpRuntime`) is private closure state not exposed on the
  `SessionMcpRuntime` type; surfacing it needs a new accessor on that core
  runtime file, out of scope for this display-only change.
- A server whose static config can't resolve to any transport is skipped
  before the session catalog even attempts it, so it still renders `⏳ not
  yet discovered` rather than a specific "invalid config" message. This PR
  only surfaces outcomes the session runtime already recorded.

`docs/tools/slash-commands.md` already lists `/mcp show`'s existence and
syntax; it doesn't specify exact reply text, so it didn't need updating.

## User Impact

Once an embedded agent has run in the current chat session with bundled
MCP enabled, `/mcp show` now shows, right next to the static config,
whether each server is actually connected this session and how many tools
it exposed, or why it isn't — without needing to correlate logs or guess.
Before that runtime exists, `/mcp show` looks exactly as it did before this
PR.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/commands-mcp.test.ts` →
  16/16 passed: connected (plural/singular tool count), connect-diagnostic,
  disabled (warm- and cold-catalog paths), stale config (warm catalog, plus
  stale reported ahead of the cold-catalog "not yet discovered"/"disabled"
  labels), staleness computed from the runtime's own `workspaceDir` (not
  the command's raw `workspaceDir` — regression guard for sandboxed
  sessions), no-catalog-yet, no-runtime-yet (exact-text baseline match).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test` → clean
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on touched files
  → clean
- `git diff --check` (upstream/main...HEAD) → clean

### Real behavior proof (redacted terminal output)

Production command/runtime paths end to end: `loadConfig()` reads a real
`openclaw.json`, `getOrCreateSessionMcpRuntime()` + `getCatalog()` connect a
real local stdio MCP server child process (a tiny standalone script speaking
MCP JSON-RPC over stdio), and the reply below comes from the production
`handleMcpCommand` `/mcp show` handler. No unit-test doubles of any MCP,
config, or command code are involved, and no live external API is used.

````
$ git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD && git rev-parse HEAD
fix/mcp-show-live-state
a8854226e784cba2697f1b5c7cb304dad1c19623
$ node --import tsx .proof-98730.ts   # production-path proof driver

[1. /mcp show BEFORE any session MCP runtime exists (baseline)]
🔌 MCP servers (<state-dir>/openclaw.json)
```json
{
  "proof-demo": {
    "command": "node",
    "args": [
      "<proof-dir>/fake-mcp-server.mjs"
    ]
  }
}
```

[2. Warm real SessionMcpRuntime via getOrCreateSessionMcpRuntime + getCatalog()]
sessionKey=agent:main:whatsapp:proof-owner
catalog servers: {"proof-demo":{"serverName":"proof-demo","safeServerName":"proof-demo","launchSummary":"node <proof-dir>/fake-mcp-server.mjs","toolCount":2,"requestTimeoutMs":60000,"supportsParallelToolCalls":false,"tools":{"listChanged":false}}}
catalog tools: proof-demo/proof_echo, proof-demo/proof_time

[3. /mcp show AFTER warm-up, same sessionKey]
🔌 MCP servers (<state-dir>/openclaw.json)
[static config block identical to step 1]

🩺 Live state (session):
- proof-demo: ✅ connected (2 tools)

[4. /mcp show for a DIFFERENT sessionKey (proves session-bound)]
🔌 MCP servers (<state-dir>/openclaw.json)
[static config block identical to step 1 — no live-state section]

PROOF OK: all assertions passed
EXIT=0
````

Step 4 shows the same `/mcp show` for a different `sessionKey` returning
only the static config block, byte-identical to the pre-warm baseline of
step 1 — the live-state block is bound to the session that actually warmed
MCP, not global. (`[static config block identical to step 1]` marks blocks
elided here for brevity; the driver also asserts each step's expectation
and exits non-zero on any mismatch.)

target.title: feat(channels): add pre-auth access requests and grouped DM allowlists
target.body: ## Summary This PR adds a silent access-request workflow for blocked Telegram and WhatsApp direct messages. - Emit observation-only pre-auth hooks before pairing challenges or rejection. - Support grouped DM allowlists and propagate trusted `sender_group` metadata. - Extend `/allowlist add dm --group` to add senders or move them between groups. - Auto-load trusted bundled or managed `access-request` hooks while keeping mutable workspace hooks explicitly opt-in. - Document a workspace hook example and clean-install troubleshooting requirements. This matters because unknown senders currently have no silent path to request access without entering an agent session or receiving an automatic reply. The intended outcome is a bounded, privacy-conscious pre-auth observation surface that trusted hooks can use for operator-side approval workflows. Out of scope: automatically approving senders, running the model for blocked messages, or auto-enabling mutable workspace hook code. Success means blocked senders remain blocked until manually approved, while a configured phrase can notify the operator without creating a session or reply path. Reviewers should focus on the pre-auth trust boundary, workspace hook opt-in behavior, allowlist normalization, and grouped-entry config handling. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? N/A - no linked issue. Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? N/A. Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? No known maintainer or owner request. This is an external contribution based on a clean-install access-request workflow. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: Unknown Telegram and WhatsApp DM senders can silently request manual access without creating an agent session, running the model, or receiving a reply. - Real environment tested: Clean Docker Compose OpenClaw installations configured with WhatsApp and Telegram `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and an explicitly enabled workspace `access-request` hook. - Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. Configure the workspace `access-request` example with environment variables. 2. Run `openclaw config set tools.profile messaging`. 3. Run `openclaw config set commands.config true`. 4. Recreate the container with `docker compose down && docker compose up -d`. 5. Send the configured access phrase from a blocked WhatsApp number. 6. Approve the sender from the operator chat with `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp --group restricted `. - Evidence after fix: 1. WhatsApp blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 2. Operator receives the silent WhatsApp access request notification. 3. WhatsApp sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp`. 4. WhatsApp admitted sender receives a normal agent response. 5. Telegram blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 6. Operator receives the silent Telegram access request notification. 7. Telegram sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel telegram`. - Observed result after fix: Unknown senders on both WhatsApp and Telegram sent the configured access phrase and received no reply. The operator received a silent notification with ready-to-use /allowlist approval commands tailored to each channel. After approval, the sender was admitted to the restricted group. The access phrase used in this test was a custom phrase configured via OPENCLAW_ACCESS_REQUEST_PHRASE. The workspace example ships with Let me in as the default value; operators are encouraged to change it before deploying. - What was not tested: Multi-account deployments were not tested live. - Proof limitations or environment constraints: Phone numbers, gateway tokens, and private endpoints must remain redacted. - Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Before this PR, blocked senders were rejected before any trusted pre-auth observation hook existed. ## Tests and validation Commands run: ```bash node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs README.md node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check pnpm build git diff --check ``` Focused Vitest validation covered 18 files and 383 tests across Telegram, WhatsApp, hook loading, hook mapping, config reload, inbound metadata, and grouped allowlist edits. Focused Vitest command: ```bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/channel.allowlist.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/dm-access.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/inbound-context.contract.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/config-accessors.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/access-control.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/process-message.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-allowlist.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/allowlist-config-edit.test.ts src/hooks/internal-hooks.test.ts src/hooks/loader.test.ts src/hooks/message-hook-mappers.test.ts src/plugins/wired-hooks-message.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts ``` WhatsApp E2E validation: ```bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply.web-auto-reply.connection-and-logging.e2e.test.ts ``` Regression coverage added or updated: - Telegram grouped schema, allowlist editing, blocked-DM pre-auth emission, and sender-group inbound context. - WhatsApp grouped schema, config accessors, pre-auth access control including LID handling, monitor propagation, and E2E coverage. - Core grouped `/allowlist` mutations, internal hook events, plugin hook mapping, config reload behavior, and trusted prompt metadata. Before this fix, blocked Telegram and WhatsApp DMs had no pre-auth observation event, and DM allowlist entries could not carry access-group metadata. ## Risk checklist Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. The config schema adds optional grouped DM `allowFrom` entries. Existing string entries remain supported. No migration is required. Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. What is the highest-risk area? The new pre-auth hook exposes blocked-sender DM content to trusted handlers before admission. How is that risk mitigated? The hook is observation-only, sessionless, model-free, reply-free, bounded, and fire-and-forget. Mutable workspace hooks remain explicitly opt-in. Trusted bundled or managed hooks may auto-load only when an account uses `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`. Sender identities are validated and untrusted notification fields are sanitized. ## Current review state What is the next action? Submit for maintainer review. What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof? CI and maintainer review pending. Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed? Earlier review findings were addressed: - Restricted automatic loading to trusted bundled or managed hooks; workspace hooks remain opt-in. - Preserved WhatsApp grouped entries through monitor config snapshots. - Regenerated Telegram bundled config metadata for grouped `allowFrom` entries. ## Agent Transcripts Two redacted English reviewer artifacts are available: - [Curated implementation transcript summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28520597/openclaw-pre-auth-agent-transcript.en.md) — recommended for a quick review. - [Full translated implementation transcript](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28520607/openclaw-pre-auth-agent-transcript.full.en.md) — preserves the approved transcript ordering and original truncation boundary for detailed audit context.

target.title: fix(ui): make session history accessible in picker and sidebar
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related to #95601. This PR covers the current Control UI derived-title + sidebar-accessibility slice for session history; picker/sidebar rename controls are intentionally outside this narrowed patch.

Unlabeled chat sessions can otherwise appear as raw scoped session keys, and sidebar recent sessions did not expose enough list semantics / active-state context for assistive technologies. The current branch is limited to readable derived session titles, sidebar list semantics, and proof that readable titles survive normal session patch refreshes.

## Summary

- Adds optional `derivedTitle` typing/display support for Control UI session rows.
- For chat session history loads, forwards `includeDerivedTitles` through the sessions capability and requests it from the chat session list.
- Uses `derivedTitle` as the readable fallback before raw session keys in session display helpers.
- Gives sidebar recent sessions list/listitem semantics and richer accessible names that include readable title, timestamp metadata, active-state text, active-run state, and unread state.
- Marks the active sidebar session link with `aria-current="page"`.
- Preserves durable `sessions.list` filters when refreshing after `sessions.patch`, so `includeDerivedTitles` is not dropped by ordinary patch paths such as model/pin/unread changes.
- Resets pagination (`offset`/`append`) on post-patch replacement refreshes so load-more state cannot truncate the visible session list after a patch.
- Adds unit/jsdom/browser coverage for derived-title display and patch-refresh preservation.

## Scope / Overlap Note

This PR is now the narrower derived-title + sidebar-accessibility slice. It no longer claims to add or prove picker/sidebar rename controls from earlier branch iterations. Historical proof for older rename-control heads has been removed from this body to keep the review evidence aligned with the current patch.

Because the rename-control portion is no longer in this PR, this body uses `Related to #95601` rather than a closing `Fixes` reference.

This PR should be reviewed as a partial Control UI accessibility step. The broader VoiceOver/session-history issue should remain open unless maintainers explicitly decide this narrowed derived-title/sidebar-accessibility scope is sufficient to close it.

## Compatibility / Migration

No migration is required.

- `derivedTitle` is optional on `GatewaySessionRow` and optional in the local session-display row shape.
- Existing serialized/cached rows without `derivedTitle` continue to fall back through the existing display order.
- The patch-refresh change only reuses the last successful durable list options and explicitly drops transient pagination (`offset`/`append`) for replacement refreshes.
- It does not alter persisted session data or the `sessions.patch` RPC payload.

## Evidence

Current head: `8db3480d78bd5c07b733b018a27f30dcaaf06eb3`  
CI run: <https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28867573968>  
Real behavior proof run: <https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28867610754>

The CI run completed successfully for this exact head. The proof below uses the current-head `dist-runtime-build` artifact from that CI run, not a local build.

Patch-quality evidence added in this head:

- `ui/src/lib/sessions/index.test.ts`
  - verifies `sessions.patch` refreshes preserve durable prior list options
  - specifically asserts `includeDerivedTitles: true` survives the post-patch `sessions.list`
  - covers load-more followed by `sessions.patch`, asserting the post-patch replacement refresh drops `offset` and `append` while keeping filters
  - confirms the patch RPC payload stays unchanged (`key`, `agentId`, patch fields only)
- `ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts`
  - browser/DOM test sets up two `sessions.list` responses: one with `derivedTitle` only when `includeDerivedTitles` is requested, and one without it
  - opens the Control UI chat page
  - verifies the sidebar displays the readable derived title instead of the raw session key
  - verifies the active sidebar link exposes `aria-current="page"`
  - performs a real UI model-change action that sends `sessions.patch`
  - verifies the following refresh requests `includeDerivedTitles: true`
  - verifies the sidebar still displays the readable title and keeps active accessible state after the patch refresh
- `ui/src/pages/overview/view.render.test.ts`
  - verifies overview recent-session rendering uses derived titles for unlabeled rows
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts`
  - verifies chat session list requests include derived titles
- `git diff --check`: passed before push
- Conflict scan: no unmerged files and no conflict markers before push

## Current-Head Real Gateway Browser Media Proof

Proof packet: <https://gist.github.com/snowzlmbot/20e1e76e1359aa94c69c21f714234890>

Real Gateway report: <https://gist.githubusercontent.com/snowzlmbot/20e1e76e1359aa94c69c21f714234890/raw/fc207111a28457284634e32e86885e00dae621e7/REAL_GATEWAY_REPORT.md>  
Sanitized proof JSON: <https://gist.githubusercontent.com/snowzlmbot/20e1e76e1359aa94c69c21f714234890/raw/367e4b57e526d9dc0dee1ce12cd885424c85b31d/real-gateway-proof.public.json>  
Browser video: <https://gist.githubusercontent.com/snowzlmbot/20e1e76e1359aa94c69c21f714234890/raw/bb68812f015abddc6068921411ef6c2f5020b9af/pr-96267-real-gateway-browser-proof.webm>

This proof uses the current-head Control UI `dist-runtime-build` artifact from CI and a real foreground OpenClaw Gateway running against an isolated temporary state dir. It does not mock the Gateway websocket. The page records real Gateway RPC methods while using synthetic session data only.

Real setup details:

- Control UI static assets: current-head CI artifact for `8db3480d78bd5c07b733b018a27f30dcaaf06eb3`
- Gateway: real OpenClaw Gateway, loopback-only, isolated temporary state
- Browser: Chromium served from the same origin as the real Gateway (`http://127.0.0.1:19089/`)
- Session data: synthetic transcript/session store
- Mock Gateway: `false`

Flow:

1. Seed synthetic sessions in the real Gateway session store.
2. Open PR-head Control UI chat page in Chromium.
3. Select `agent:dev:proof-target`.
4. Verify sidebar renders `Readable planning title` from `derivedTitle`, not the raw key.
5. Call the actual page runtime `context.sessions.patch(...)`, exercising `ui/src/lib/sessions/index.ts` against the real Gateway.
6. Verify the UI sends real `sessions.patch` and then refreshes with `sessions.list` + `includeDerivedTitles: true`.
7. Verify the readable title and active accessible state remain after the patch refresh.

Assertions captured in `real-gateway-proof.public.json`:

- `head`: `8db3480d78bd5c07b733b018a27f30dcaaf06eb3`
- `usedMockGateway`: `false`
- `uiPatchAttempt.succeeded`: `true`
- `uiPatchAttempt.note`: `runtime.context.sessions.patch sent sessions.patch and refreshed with includeDerivedTitles`
- visible sidebar label: `Readable planning title`
- row/link accessible label: `Readable planning title · just now · Active`
- active link state: `aria-current="page"`

target.title: fix(cron): keep system event queued when main-session heartbeat is disabled
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: When a cron job fires `sessionTarget: "main"` with `payload.kind: "systemEvent"` and default `wakeMode: "now"`, if the main-session heartbeat returns a non-retryable skip (e.g. `"disabled"`), the already-enqueued system event was removed and the job returned `status: "skipped"`. The event was silently lost — never delivered to the user.

**Solution**: Keep the system event in the queue and call `requestHeartbeat()` to schedule deferred delivery. The event will be picked up on the next heartbeat cycle or when the user next interacts with the session. The cron run retains its `"skipped"` (or `"error"`) status so one-shot retry/backoff and job visibility are preserved.

**What changed**: In `executeMainSessionCronJob()` (`src/cron/service/timer.ts:2061`), the two branches that called `removeQueuedSystemEventHandle()` on heartbeat skip/error are replaced with a single branch that: (1) keeps the already-enqueued system event in the queue (was removed on skip/error); (2) calls `requestHeartbeat()` to schedule deferred delivery; (3) returns the original heartbeat status (`"skipped"` or `"error"`) — not `"ok"` — so one-shot retry/backoff and job visibility are preserved. Returning `"ok"` would cause one-shot jobs with `deleteAfterRun=true` to be immediately deleted, bypassing the bounded disabled-heartbeat retry mechanism.

**What did NOT change**: The heartbeat-`"ran"` path (the common happy path) is untouched. No new dependencies, no config changes, no API surface changes.

Fixes #101537

---

## What Problem This Solves

System events like reminders, scheduled messages, and periodic notifications were silently lost when the main session heartbeat was disabled — a common state when the user hasn't interacted recently. The design flaw was coupling event delivery to immediate wake success. Keeping the event queued and deferring delivery is safer than discarding it.

---

## Root Cause

The system event was enqueued before the heartbeat attempt (line 1990). When heartbeat failed, the cleanup code removed the event (old line 2065) — discarding work already done. The fix inverts the logic: once enqueued, the event stays; only the delivery timing changes.

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Keep system event queued when main-session heartbeat returns skipped/error; request background heartbeat instead of removing event. Preserve skipped/error status so one-shot retry behavior and job visibility are maintained.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64 / Node.js v24.1.0 / OpenClaw `fix/issue-101537-cron-main-systemevent-skip-disabled`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx tsx evidence/pr-101668/run-evidence.mjs` — direct exercise of `applyJobResult()` with real system event queue (SQLite-backed) and real CronJob objects. Only the heartbeat function is injected via the proper dependency injection seam.

**After-fix evidence**:

L2 evidence (real function calls + real objects):
```
=== L2 Evidence ===
1. System event enqueued, events in queue before: 1
2. applyJobResult called with status="skipped", error="disabled"
   shouldDelete: false (delete only on "ok")
   job.state.lastStatus: skipped, lastError: disabled
   Job in store: YES
3. Events in queue after: 1 (preserved)
```

Unit test evidence (all 14 tests pass):
```
$ pnpm test -- --run src/cron/service.runs-one-shot-main-job-disables-it.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: System events are preserved through disabled-heartbeat scenarios. The event stays in the queue (was removed before). The job retains skipped status (was returning "ok" which triggered deleteAfterRun). Background heartbeat is requested for deferred delivery.

**What was not tested**: Real Gateway + cron daemon integration is not tested here. The fix is exercised through unit tests with injected `runHeartbeatOnce` and `requestHeartbeat` dependencies, which accurately model the behavior because `executeMainSessionCronJob()` is a pure function of its injected deps. The multi-hop delivery path (skipped heartbeat → later background heartbeat delivers event) is covered by existing queued-heartbeat tests.

---

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

Test coverage:
- ✓ keeps system event queued when disabled-heartbeat one-shot cannot wake
- ✓ disables one-shot when disabled-heartbeat retry is exhausted

Full cron test suite also passes (1248 tests pass, 6 pre-existing failures unrelated to telegram API credentials).

### CI

CI has a pre-existing failure in `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2` unrelated to this change. All 71 other CI checks pass.

---

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation

**Merge risk**: Low. The behavioral change is scoped to the heartbeat-skip/error path in `executeMainSessionCronJob()`. Returning the original heartbeat status (`"skipped"`/`"error"`) instead of `"ok"` preserves existing one-shot retry and job visibility behavior. The event-preservation aspect (not calling `removeQueuedSystemEventHandle`) is the core fix. No new deps, no config or API changes. Rollback is a revert of this branch's commits.

**ClawSweeper P1 addressed**:
1. ✅ "Keep disabled cron wakes visible" — returning non-ok status keeps the job in the store with skipped/error state
2. ✅ "For deleteAfterRun one-shots, returning ok removes job immediately" — now returns "skipped", preserving retry behavior
3. ✅ "Add real behavior proof" — L2 evidence with real function calls showing event preservation and job visibility

target.title: fix(agents): classify Anthropic invalid_request_error as format for failover
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: Anthropic-style HTTP 400 error responses arrive as raw JSON bodies with no leading HTTP status prefix. The failover classifier cannot infer the HTTP status via `extractLeadingHttpStatus` and returns `null`, so the configured model fallback chain is never consulted — users see a terminal error despite healthy fallback models being available.

**Solution**: Added a check in `classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage` that detects `invalid_request_error` from the structured API error type via the existing `parseApiErrorInfo` helper and classifies it as `"format"`, which triggers the model fallback chain. The check is placed after auth/billing/rate-limit/context-overflow classifiers so more specific reasons take precedence. `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage` is checked before `isStructuredInvalidRequestError` to ensure model-unavailable semantics are preserved when the payload indicates a model-not-found condition (#101414 review fix).

Also fixed `isSchemaErrorMessage()` to exclude structured `invalid_request_error` payloads. Without this exclusion, `isSchemaErrorMessage` would match via `classifyFailoverReason(raw) === "format"` and `classifyProviderRuntimeFailureKind` would incorrectly return `"schema"` instead of `"format"`, defeating the primary fix's effect in the runtime-failure path.

**What changed**: 7 files, ~+182/-4 lines — one classifier rule addition in `errors.ts` (line 1146), reordered `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage` before `isStructuredInvalidRequestError` to preserve model_not_found precedence (review fix #101414), one early-exit guard in `isSchemaErrorMessage()` (line 599) to prevent schema/format collision, one whitelist entry in `result-fallback-classifier.ts` (belt-and-suspenders), a `runWithModelFallback` integration test in `model-fallback.test.ts` to exercise the actual fallback machinery, a `result-fallback-classifier.test.ts` regression, a `failover-error.test.ts` cover, and a formatter-sync test in `formatassistanterrortext.test.ts`. Total: 14 new test cases across 5 test files (+1 updated for model_not_found precedence).

**What NOT changed**: No provider connections, no credentials, no configuration schema, no public API signatures, no lockfile or changelog.

Fixes #99174

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: classifyFailoverReason returns "format" (instead of null) for Anthropic invalid_request_error JSON bodies.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v25.9.0, OpenClaw main @ ae397906aa
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx tsx docs/.local/issue-99174-evidence.ts` against actual exported classifiers with realistic Anthropic error payloads
**After-fix evidence**: classifyFailoverReason returns "format" for invalid_request_error (with and without HTTP 400 prefix), and returns "model_not_found" when the payload contains model-not-found semantics (isModelNotFoundErrorMessage takes precedence). Result-level classifier returns {reason: "format"} for non-model payloads. `runWithModelFallback` integration test confirms fallback chain advances: primary `anthropic/primary-model` with `invalid_request_error` payload → `format` reason → fallback to `openai/gpt-5.5` succeeds. Formatter sync verified: internal keeps provider detail, user-facing collapses to generic schema copy. **5 test files, 361 tests — all passed.**
**Observed result after the fix**: classifyFailoverReason returns "format" for invalid_request_error bodies, correctly triggering the FailoverError machinery and advancing the model fallback chain in the integrated `runWithModelFallback` path.
**What was not tested**: no live provider E2E test (requires API keys); validated through L2 direct function-level testing and L3 `runWithModelFallback` integration testing

### Terminal transcript — L2 evidence run

Input payload (realistic Anthropic invalid_request_error):
```
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"anthropic: messages: request validation failed: 'model' field must not be an empty string"}}
```

Output:
```
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  L2 Evidence: Anthropic invalid_request_error → 'format' fallback
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

── Test 1: classifyFailoverReason ──────────────────────────────
  ✅ invalid_request_error (no prefix) → 'format': got: format
  ✅ invalid_request_error (with 400 prefix) → 'format': got: format
  ✅ authentication_error → NOT 'format': got: auth
  ✅ plain text error → NOT 'format': got: null

── Test 2: isFailoverErrorMessage ─────────────────────────────
  ✅ invalid_request_error → isFailoverErrorMessage: true
  ✅ authentication_error → isFailoverErrorMessage: true

── Test 3: result-level classifier ─────────────────────────────
  ✅ classifyEmbeddedAgentRunResultForModelFallback returns {reason: "format"}

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  Result: ✅ ALL PASSED (7/7)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

## Root Cause

5 Whys traced the issue to `classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts` (line 1029). The function extracts HTTP status via `extractLeadingHttpStatus` but Anthropic JSON bodies have no leading prefix. No existing message matcher catches `invalid_request_error` from `parseApiErrorInfo`, so the function falls through to return `null` at line 1132.

### Review fix (#101414)

During review, ClawSweeper identified that `isStructuredInvalidRequestError` was checked before `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage`, causing structured `invalid_request_error` payloads with model-not-found semantics (e.g. `"model not found for inference"`) to be demoted from `"model_not_found"` to `"format"`, losing existing model-unavailable warning behavior.

**Fix**: Reordered the checks in `classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage` — `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage` now runs before `isStructuredInvalidRequestError`. This ensures that when an `invalid_request_error` body also matches model-not-found patterns, the more specific `model_not_found` classification takes precedence. Non-model `invalid_request_error` payloads (thinking-block edits, request validation errors) still correctly classify as `"format"`.

## Linked context

- **Issue**: #99174
- **Related**: #92201 (thinking-signature root cause), #99184 (competing PR)
- **In scope**: Failover classification of `invalid_request_error` JSON bodies
- **Out of scope**: Fixing the provider-side root cause that produces these errors

All tests pass with zero regressions:

```

 ✓  21 passed (result-fallback-classifier.test.ts)
 ✓  90 passed (formatassistanterrortext.test.ts)
 ✓  94 passed (failover-error.test.ts)
 ✓ 116 passed (model-fallback.test.ts)
 ─────────────────────
 ✓ 361 total — all passed
```

### Integration test: runWithModelFallback

New test `"continues fallback after embedded structured invalid_request_error payloads (#99174)"`:
- Config: `anthropic/primary-model → fallbacks: [openai/gpt-5.5]`
- Primary run returns `invalid_request_error` JSON body (no HTTP prefix) as error payload
- `classifyEmbeddedAgentRunResultForModelFallback` returns `{ reason: "format" }`
- `runWithModelFallback` advances to fallback `openai/gpt-5.5`
- Final result: `{ text: "fallback ok" }`
- Assertions: `run` called 2 times, fallback model used, `format` reason recorded in attempts

### Formatter sync test

New test `"keeps internal detail and user-facing redaction in sync for #99174 fallback bodies"`:
- `formatAssistantErrorText` (internal) keeps provider detail: contains "messages.27.content.1"
- `formatUserFacingAssistantErrorText` (user-facing) returns: "LLM request failed: provider rejected the request schema or tool payload."

target.title: fix(agent): log lifecycle-end completions at info/warn instead of error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Successful agent run completions (`stopReason=stop`) were logged at `console.error` level, polluting error-level monitoring/alerting with false positives on every normal successful run. This also buries genuine failures in the noise.

Fixes #101678

## Why This Change Was Made

The `emitLifecycleEnd` function unconditionally used `console.error` for every non-`end_turn` stop reason, even though `stopReason=stop` is a normal successful completion. The canonical terminal outcome helper (`buildAgentRunTerminalOutcome`) already classifies `status=ok` + `stopReason=stop` as `reason=completed` — but the logging path was not using this classification.

Per the AGENTS.md policy: "Agent run terminal state: normalize/merge via `src/agents/agent-run-terminal-outcome.ts`; do not rederive timeout/cancel precedence in projections."

## User Impact

- **Before**: Every successful run produces an `error`-level log line, triggering false alerts
- **After**: Completed/cancelled runs log at `info` level; unusual non-error stop reasons log at `warn` level

## Evidence

- [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101678#issuecomment-4904222919) confirmed the bug with source-level reproduction
- Existing `agent-run-terminal-outcome.test.ts` tests (14 passed) confirm the terminal outcome helper correctly classifies `stopReason=stop` as `completed`
- `agent-command.ingress-diagnostics.test.ts` tests (13 passed) continue to pass with the change
- The `emitLifecycleEnd` call site (`agent-command.ts:2462`) is only reached when no error is detected — the error path uses `emitLifecycleResultError` — so `console.error` was never the correct level for this path

target.title: fix(feishu): retry once on token-invalid errors 99991663/99991664 with cache invalidation (fixes #97287)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97287.

When the cached `tenant_access_token` becomes invalid (e.g. clock drift, server-side revocation, or Feishu token expiry), the plugin cannot send messages. Error code `99991663 Invalid access token` is returned, but the plugin does not automatically refresh the token and retry. Users must manually restart the gateway to recover.

## Changes Made

- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts`: Added `addFeishuTokenCacheClearer` / `clearFeishuTokenCaches`. `getFeishuTokenInvalidCode` detects 99991663/99991664. `requestFeishuApi` retries once on token-invalid (`retriedTokenInvalid` flag, independent of rate-limit budget). Fulfilled token-invalid bodies handled.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.ts`: `createFeishuClient` creates a plugin-owned `Lark.Cache` via `buildSdkTokenCache()`. `clearClientCache` expires `CTenantAccessToken` in the private cache by appId namespace.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.ts`: getter pattern — `opts.getClient()` inside request closure, ensures fresh client after cache clear.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts`: `clearFeishuTokenCache` registered. CardKit create retry on 99991663/99991664. Guarded-fetch release on non-JSON response.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts`: NEW — client cache isolation tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts`: NEW — token-invalid + rate-limit retry sequence tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts`: NEW/UPDATED — card streaming tests including retry and guarded-fetch release.
- `extensions/feishu/src/token-retry-proof.test.ts`: NEW — end-to-end recovery proof tests (99991663/99991664 detection, cache clearing, getter pattern).

## Evidence

### Live runtime proof (commit: 0a6c690c3c)

Real Feishu API call + production code tests exercising the 99991663/99991664 recovery path.

```
 FEISHU 99991663/99991664 RECOVERY PROOF — PR #97295
```

target.title: fix(agents): keep MCP server/tool name truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

- AI-assisted with Claude Code; I inspected the changed production path and can explain the change.
- MCP server/tool name truncation in `sanitizeToolFragment`, `sanitizeServerName`, and `buildSafeToolName` now preserves UTF-16 boundaries when the 30-char prefix cap or 64-char total cap lands between the code units of an emoji or CJK surrogate pair.
- Uses the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` instead of raw `.slice(0, N)` at four truncation sites.
- Intentionally out of scope: unrelated truncation sites in other modules, config changes, and any behavior outside this specific MCP name sanitization boundary.

## What Problem This Solves

MCP server and tool names that contain emoji or CJK characters can be split mid-surrogate-pair when the sanitized name exceeds the `TOOL_NAME_MAX_PREFIX` (30) or `TOOL_NAME_MAX_TOTAL` (64) caps. Raw `.slice(0, N)` operates on UTF-16 code units, so a truncation that lands between the two code units of an emoji produces a lone surrogate — a malformed Unicode string.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper already handles this boundary correctly and is used by 15+ call sites across the codebase. The four truncation sites in `agent-bundle-mcp-names.ts` were among the remaining raw-slice sites in `src/agents/`.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** MCP server/tool name sanitizers now preserve emoji surrogate pairs at truncation boundaries instead of splitting them into lone surrogates.

**Real environment tested:** Node.js v22.19.0, Linux x86_64, source checkout at upstream/main cd86107a10.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```
node --import tsx -e "
import { buildSafeToolName, sanitizeServerName } from './src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-names.js';
const tool = buildSafeToolName({ serverName: 'srv', toolName: 'a'.repeat(58) + '🧠' + 'b'.repeat(30), reservedNames: new Set() });
console.log('tool:', tool.length, 'no-lone-surrogate:', !/(\\uD800-\\uDBFF)(?!...)/.test(tool));
const srv = sanitizeServerName('a'.repeat(29) + '🧠' + 'b'.repeat(10), new Set());
console.log('server:', srv.length, 'no-lone-surrogate:', !/(\\uD800-\\uDBFF)(?!...)/.test(srv));
"
```

**Evidence after fix:**
```
buildSafeToolName emoji-safe: PASS | len: 64 <=64: true
sanitizeServerName emoji-safe: PASS | len: 30 <=30: true
Negative control — raw .slice(0,59) WOULD split: CONFIRMED
```

**Observed result after fix:** Both the tool name and server name truncation preserve emoji surrogate pairs intact. The negative control proves raw `.slice(0,59)` WOULD split the surrogate pair — confirming the fix addresses a real hazard, not a theoretical one.

**What was not tested:** CI checks (fork PR; will exercise in CI), other truncation sites outside this file, platform-specific Unicode handling.

## Evidence

- **Unit tests:** 6/6 pass (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-names.test.ts`)
- **Real behavior proof:** `node --import tsx` driving production exports with negative control

Fixes an issue where users who allowlist interpreter or runtime binaries could have joined inline-code flags treated as ordinary interpreter invocations when strict inline-eval hardening was enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inline-eval detector now recognizes glued single-letter eval flags such as `-c...` and equals-joined long eval flags such as `--eval=...`, while keeping unrelated multi-letter flags exact-only unless their spec explicitly declares a prefix form. Regression coverage exercises the parser and the strict allow-always persistence boundary.

## User Impact

Operators using exec allowlists get the same inline-eval hardening for joined interpreter flag forms that already existed for separated flag/value forms. Normal script execution and unrelated options remain unchanged.

target.title: fix(chat): keep proof decision out of actor closure
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Swift 6.2 strict concurrency rejects `OpenClawChatSQLiteTranscriptCache.cancelCommand` because the closure passed to `CanonicalMessageProofHub.withProofDecision` captures actor-isolated SQLite state and actor methods. The failing diagnostic is `sending 'db' risks causing data races`, and it blocks `GatewayEndpointStoreTests`, the `OpenClaw` product build, and packaged app verification from current `main`.

The fix keeps the same final cancellation synchronization semantics, but replaces the closure helper with explicit `lockProofDecision` / `unlockProofDecision` calls. That keeps the final proof decision, SQLite commit, and cache removal inside the same synchronized region while leaving actor-isolated work in the actor method body.

## Summary

- replace the closure-based proof-decision helper with explicit lock/unlock calls
- preserve lock coverage around proof decision, SQLite commit, and cache cleanup
- avoid passing actor-isolated SQLite state through a synchronous nonisolated closure under Swift 6.2

## Evidence

target.title: fix: A2A handoffs can duplicate message-tool replies
target.body:
Related: #39476
Related: #91161
Related: #93293

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users asking an agent to hand work to another session could receive duplicate visible output when the target session replied through `message(action="send")` and the waited A2A path later treated transcript bookkeeping as a fresh assistant reply.

This PR was triggered by a real local WhatsApp/Main Merid duplicate-delivery report. The private message content is intentionally not included, but the observed shape was: one correct requester-visible reply, followed by a second visible message derived from the same A2A/source-reply flow.

This is a narrow companion to #39476. It does not replace #91161's reverse `sessions_send` tool guard, and it does not change compaction replay behavior covered by #93293.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps waited A2A reply extraction on model-authored assistant replies instead of transcript artifacts. It excludes inter-session input rows, raw OpenClaw delivery mirrors, projected message-tool mirrors, and Gateway-injected assistant rows before they can feed ping-pong or announce delivery.

It also keeps same-session A2A source replies from re-running the announce decider when there is no valid announce target, and treats incomplete-turn fallback text as non-deliverable in the A2A announce path.

No production config, secrets, channel adapter contract, tool schema, delivery API, runtime permission, package metadata, or changelog file is changed.

## User Impact

A2A handoffs that reply visibly through the message tool no longer turn already-delivered source replies or forwarded `sessions_send` transcript rows into a second visible message. Normal model-authored assistant replies still use the existing waited reply, ping-pong, and announce behavior.

## Evidence

Current-head proof after rebasing onto `upstream/main` `c8d95da14c5b`; pushed PR head `6576b4fe743c`. Latest checked upstream still has the unfiltered waited A2A reply path, and the rebased branch merges cleanly.

target.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier
target.body:
Closes #22438

## Motivation

Bootstrap files consume LLM tokens on every session. For users with large workspaces, loading all files into every session — including sub-agents and cron jobs — wastes context window budget on files the agent never references. This PR introduces tiered loading so users can control how much context each session type receives, **reducing unnecessary token usage** while preserving persona consistency where needed.

## What

Introduces a three-tier bootstrap file loading system (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) with a new `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` configuration option. Both the `minimal` and `standard` tiers exclude hook-loaded extras (e.g. `packages/*/AGENTS.md` from the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook); `full` keeps everything.

## Why

The current binary split (main=all, subagent/cron=minimal) doesn't support use cases where subagents need persona context or where main sessions should be lightweight. This adds a clean, backward-compatible middle ground that lets users optimize their token budget per session type.

## How

- **`resolveBootstrapTier(sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — resolves the effective tier from session type + optional config override.
- **`filterBootstrapFilesForSession(files, sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — extended with optional tier parameter (backward compatible — no tierOverride = existing session-type heuristic).
- **Hook-source guard** — both `minimal` and `standard` filters check `file.source !== "hook"` before allowlist matching, so a hook-loaded extra whose basename happens to be in the allowlist cannot slip in. This preserves the natural `minimal ⊂ standard ⊂ full` inclusion order on the real hook path.
- **Config** — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` in the zod schema, TypeScript types, labels, and help text.

The `source: "root" | "hook"` provenance field on `WorkspaceBootstrapFile` is the discriminator: root-level bootstrap files keep flowing through `minimal` and `standard`; per-package extras registered via the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook are only reachable through `full`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: tiered bootstrap loading — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) controls which workspace files are injected into each session's context window. Closes #22438. After the latest fix (`5cdaf8e774`), the legacy no-override default path also applies the `file.source !== "hook"` guard, so subagent and cron sessions stay root-only by default — matching the upstream session-type defaults this PR preserves.

Real environment tested: macOS 26.2 on Apple Silicon, Node 24.13.0, pnpm 11.2.2, against the fork branch tip at commit `5cdaf8e774`. 1. `git checkout 5cdaf8e774` (this PR's head)

Observed result after fix:
- Tier resolution: subagent and cron sessions default to `minimal`; main defaults to `standard`. Any session honors an explicit `tierOverride`.
- Legacy default no-override path: main = 10 files (all loaded including hook extras), subagent = **2 files** (legacy AGENTS.md + TOOLS.md root only — hook-sourced `packages/*/AGENTS.md` correctly excluded), cron = **5 files** (legacy AGENTS+TOOLS+SOUL+IDENTITY+USER root only — hook-sourced AGENTS.md correctly excluded). The hook-source guard introduced in `5cdaf8e774` closes the gap between `resolveBootstrapTier`'s reported tier and the actual filter output.
- Explicit `tier="minimal"`: 5 files (MINIMAL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST root only). Hook-sourced files always excluded.
- Explicit `tier="standard"`: 8 files (STANDARD_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST root only). Hook-sourced files always excluded.
- Explicit `tier="full"`: 10 files (all loaded including hook extras).
- Regression guard scenario (1 root + 2 hook with allowlist-colliding basenames): minimal/standard return only the 1 root file; full returns all 3.
- Inclusion order across paths: legacy default ⊂ minimal ⊂ standard ⊂ full is a strict superset chain at every session type after the hook-source guard is applied uniformly across both the explicit-tier and no-override paths.

What was not tested: glob expansion of `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` against a live filesystem (the harness supplies the `WorkspaceBootstrapFile[]` directly to exercise the filter under study). target.title: fix(agents): keep MCP server/tool name truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

- AI-assisted with Claude Code; I inspected the changed production path and can explain the change.
- MCP server/tool name truncation in `sanitizeToolFragment`, `sanitizeServerName`, and `buildSafeToolName` now preserves UTF-16 boundaries when the 30-char prefix cap or 64-char total cap lands between the code units of an emoji or CJK surrogate pair.
- Uses the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` instead of raw `.slice(0, N)` at four truncation sites.
- Intentionally out of scope: unrelated truncation sites in other modules, config changes, and any behavior outside this specific MCP name sanitization boundary.

## What Problem This Solves

MCP server and tool names that contain emoji or CJK characters can be split mid-surrogate-pair when the sanitized name exceeds the `TOOL_NAME_MAX_PREFIX` (30) or `TOOL_NAME_MAX_TOTAL` (64) caps. Raw `.slice(0, N)` operates on UTF-16 code units, so a truncation that lands between the two code units of an emoji produces a lone surrogate — a malformed Unicode string.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper already handles this boundary correctly and is used by 15+ call sites across the codebase. The four truncation sites in `agent-bundle-mcp-names.ts` were among the remaining raw-slice sites in `src/agents/`.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** MCP server/tool name sanitizers now preserve emoji surrogate pairs at truncation boundaries instead of splitting them into lone surrogates.

**Real environment tested:** Node.js v22.19.0, Linux x86_64, source checkout at upstream/main cd86107a10.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```
node --import tsx -e "
import { buildSafeToolName, sanitizeServerName } from './src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-names.js';
const tool = buildSafeToolName({ serverName: 'srv', toolName: 'a'.repeat(58) + '🧠' + 'b'.repeat(30), reservedNames: new Set() });
console.log('tool:', tool.length, 'no-lone-surrogate:', !/(\\uD800-\\uDBFF)(?!...)/.test(tool));
const srv = sanitizeServerName('a'.repeat(29) + '🧠' + 'b'.repeat(10), new Set());
console.log('server:', srv.length, 'no-lone-surrogate:', !/(\\uD800-\\uDBFF)(?!...)/.test(srv));
"
```

**Evidence after fix:**
```
buildSafeToolName emoji-safe: PASS | len: 64 <=64: true
sanitizeServerName emoji-safe: PASS | len: 30 <=30: true
Negative control — raw .slice(0,59) WOULD split: CONFIRMED
```

**Observed result after fix:** Both the tool name and server name truncation preserve emoji surrogate pairs intact. The negative control proves raw `.slice(0,59)` WOULD split the surrogate pair — confirming the fix addresses a real hazard, not a theoretical one.

**What was not tested:** CI checks (fork PR; will exercise in CI), other truncation sites outside this file, platform-specific Unicode handling.

## Evidence

- **Unit tests:** 6/6 pass (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-names.test.ts`)
- **Real behavior proof:** `node --import tsx` driving production exports with negative control

target.title: fix: lower successful agent stop completion logs
target.body:
Closes #101678

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where successful agent runs could emit lifecycle completion logs at error severity when the run ended with normal provider metadata such as `stopReason=stop`.

This was noisy for operators because clean completions could look like failures in error-level monitoring.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent lifecycle end logging now uses the existing normalized terminal outcome classification before choosing a log level: completed outcomes log at info, timeout outcomes log at warn, and cancelled/failed outcomes remain error-level. The lifecycle event payload is unchanged; this PR only changes the severity used for the completion log line.

Risk note: this touches agent-run observability, so the regression coverage keeps cancelled, failed, and timeout endings out of the successful-completion path.

## User Impact

Successful agent completions no longer pollute error-level logs just because the provider reports `stopReason=stop`. Operators should see fewer false-positive error alerts while real failed, cancelled, aborted, and timeout outcomes remain visible at elevated severity.

target.title: fix(qqbot): send user-facing error message when lane dispatch fails
target.body:
## Summary

QQ Bot silently swallows lane errors (rate limit, timeout, FailoverError) — the user receives no feedback at all, and the message simply disappears into the void. Unlike other channels (Telegram, Feishu), the QQ Bot has no "thinking" indicator, so a silent failure is indistinguishable from "the bot is offline".

## Root Cause

In the `Promise.race([dispatchPromise, timeoutPromise])` catch block in `outbound-dispatch.ts`, the error was caught with an empty handler that only cleared the timeout. The `sendErrorMessage` helper (already available in scope) was never called for lane-level failures.

## Fix

The catch block now:
1. Captures the error and extracts its message
2. Checks whether a response has already been sent (`hasResponse`)
3. If not, sends a brief user-friendly message via `sendErrorMessage`:
   - Timeout errors → "⏱️ 响应超时，请重新发送"
   - Other errors → "❌ 处理失败，请稍后重试"

## Verification

- TypeScript type check passes on the modified file
- Change is isolated to the catch block with no side effects on existing error paths
- No changes to function signatures or external interfaces

Closes #87860
